newsitem.title: TAIWAN: FORECAST-Taiwan Dec M2 money supply -Reuters poll.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Taiwan Dec M2 money supply -Reuters poll.

text.p: The following Reuter poll of economists gives their projections for year-on-year growth in December of Taiwan's broadest money supply measure, M2.
The December indicator is due to be made public by the central bank at 0310 GMT on January 25.
November's M2 money supply growth was 8.38 percent year-on-year.
The poll results produced an average forecast for a rise of 8.30 percent in annual M2 growth in December.
Economists said they expected relatively slow M2 growth in December because of a higher year-earlier comparative base in December 1995.
"The central bank had cut banks' reserve requirements in November 1995, which triggered a higher money supply then," said Capital Securities economist Wang Chia-yuan.

The central bank last cut banks' reserve requirements in August 1996 and has largely left its macroeconomic policy levers untouched since then, although the government has tinkered with liquidity through minor open-market operations.
Wang said the overall demand for money was not strong despite relatively low interest rates, reflecting what many economists have called a real but frustratingly slow economic recovery.
